executiveSummary: Medemblik was fresh and pending when claimed: no GM0420 artifact existed and the generated manifest named task municipality_gm0420. Its official/generated 2025 identity, 45,934 residents, 61 neighbourhoods, sixteen districts, sixteen BAG woonplaatsen, 23 BRT settlement labels, ten logical road-border records and 112 scheduled-transit stop areas are substantially coherent. Neighbourhood rows total 45,930 residents, four below the municipality control (-0.009%), which the allocator reconciles without rewriting published observations. Two BAG representative points—Andijk and Medemblik—fall just outside the independently generalized CBS boundary, a retained edition/generalization warning rather than exclusion. All ten presets run deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services with finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, causal closure, service-layer invariance and monotone event burden. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The generic coastal surge asserts an exact 1.556982 m municipal flood at T+6/12/24, 21,980 affected people-equivalent and 457,998.188 deprived person-hours at T+24, then sets flood depth to exactly zero at T+48 while 20,115 people remain affected and burden reaches 1,390,963.604 by T+72. Medemblik is genuinely exposed to IJsselmeer water and primary/regional defences, but the run selects no IJsselmeer level/wind-wave boundary, defence trajectory, breach, LIWO footprint, arrival or recession; it cannot be interpreted as an official local metre prediction. The canonical Rhine/Meuse/IJssel river preset separately imposes 0.462165 m through T+72 without a locally relevant source contract. Eight nonzero single-hazard T+24 runs reuse the exact same complete neighbourhood order: coastal ranks Wervershoof Buitengebied first, Andijk Waterzuivering 43rd and Medemblik Vooroever 45th. This contradicts mechanism-specific shoreline, polder, urban-rain, heat, smoke and cyber allocation. Public evidence adds 285 partial water assets—76 surface-water pumps, five sluices, fourteen sewer pumps, 189 weirs and rwzi Wervershoof—and PWN's nationally important Andijk IJsselmeer drinking-water intake/production chain. One Liander planning sample, 86 antennas, 30 education records and external Dijklander acute care add context but not live topology, backup or restoration. A7/N307/N239/N240/N241/N505, dispersed villages, no in-boundary rail station, agriculture/glasshouse production, ports/recreation and external acute care require time-valid access and occupancy. Medemblik explicitly says its 72-hour power-outage programme is still staged: 2026 focuses on the municipal basis and support-point locations are a pilot, with further measures from 2027. Missing defence, pump, intake/quality, road, care, utility, support-point, visitor and household state remains Unknown or NoData, never safe or zero.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0420 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated CBS/BAG/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; audited 3 September 2026
supports: The annual official/generated row identifies GM0420 as Medemblik and reports 45,934 residents, density 379/km², 23.4% aged 65-plus and 6,487 one-person households. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and demographic context, not incident-time occupancy or individual vulnerability.

The municipality point [5.096689856491752,52.72234685397005] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary. The outline is suitable for selection/aggregation, not dike, polder, terrain, sewer, shoreline, route or asset connectivity.

Sixty-one neighbourhood rows in sixteen districts sum to 45,930 residents (-4, -0.009%), 19,920 households and 10,745 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. The allocator reconciles population without changing source observations.

BAG supplies sixteen woonplaatsen and BRT 23 settlement labels. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT is CC BY 4.0. Andijk and Medemblik BAG representative points fall outside the independently versioned/generalized CBS boundary; this is a review signal, not evidence those official places are outside the municipality.

evidenceSources.publisher: Hoogheemraadschap Hollands Noorderkwartier / Watermanagementcentrum Nederland / IPLO
evidenceSources.title: E02 — IJsselmeer defences, water-system semantics and LIWO scenario requirements
evidenceSources.edition: Current HHNK register page and 2025 published Medemblik–Enkhuizen/IJsselmeer legger inspected 3 September 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: HHNK distinguishes primary defences against Noordzee, Waddenzee, IJsselmeer and Markermeer from regional boezem defences and other water-retaining elevations. Its Medemblik/IJsselmeer register identifies separate defence sections and structures; they cannot be collapsed into a municipality-wide coastal scalar.

HHNK's current Medemblik work page explicitly protects Markermeer/IJsselmeer dike function, while the Westfriese Omringdijk is a 126-km historic water-defence system. Static identity and maintenance context do not publish live strength, failure, overtopping or closure.

LIWO 2025.1.6 provides professional flood layers and says interpretation requires water-manager expertise. Scenario families distinguish primary/regional failure and water-system flooding; each needs source boundary, trajectory/breach, probability, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, edition, resolution and NoData.

No selected IJsselmeer level, wind-wave setup, defence failure or connected LIWO scenario is attached to the canonical coastal run. An unselected scenario or uncovered cell remains Unknown/not selected, not zero depth or safe.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Vier Noorder Koggen drainage, local rain adaptation and partial water assets
evidenceSources.edition: Official Vier Noorder Koggen water-system decision and current HHNK pages inspected 3 September 2026; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: HHNK describes Vier Noorder Koggen Oost as roughly 6,535 hectares bounded by the A7, Zwaagdijk and IJsselmeer, drained by four pumps at Wervershoof with a stated combined 1,400 m³/minute into the IJsselmeer and supplied via six IJsselmeer inlets. These are source-document design/context values, not live available capacity.

HHNK says the modern Vier Noorder Koggen station has been fully electric since 2015 and the old steam installation can support emergencies; historical availability is not proof of automatic incident backup, fuel, staffing, connectivity or current readiness.

The partial HWH assignment contains 285 points: 189 weirs, 76 surface-water pumps, fourteen sewer pumps, five sluices and rwzi Wervershoof. Functions include supply, discharge, under-drainage and combined supply/discharge, with null and zero capacity fields. CC BY-SA 4.0 points do not establish complete topology, compatible units, telemetry, power or live state.

Current HHNK projects identify Eendenkooi and IJsbaan Wognum storage optimisation and a water-storing street package/drainage sewer in Sijbekarspel. These are project/static adaptation evidence, not an observed municipal cloudburst footprint or proof of completed T+72 capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Local climate pathways and staged 72-hour resilience programme
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal preparedness page and December 2024 Stadsplan Medemblik inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Medemblik says it is preparing for 72 hours without electricity because internet, telephony, payments and heating can also fail. In 2026 it is putting the municipal basis in order, piloting where support points should be and training the crisis organisation; further measures are planned from 2027.

The municipality advises a three-day emergency kit and says its crisis organisation provides information, reception for people unable to return home, post-incident support and continuity. This is a responsibility/intent statement, not confirmed incident locations, capacity, staff, power, water, communications or accessibility.

The 2024 city plan identifies lower parts of historic Medemblik with rain nuisance, especially near Bonifaciuskerk and Gedempt Achterom, plus drought risk for timber foundations, water-quality concerns and heat stress. It is static planning context, not a live event map.

Municipal pages/documents state publication or retrieval context but no standard reuse licence or machine incident cadence. Guidance, a pilot and planned works must not be represented as completed or active operational state.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Andijk IJsselmeer drinking-water production and cross-regional dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator page and January 2026 Klimaatbuffer IJsselmeer scoping document inspected 3 September 2026
supports: PWN calls Andijk one of its most important drinking-water production locations. It takes IJsselmeer water, produces drinking water for much of West-Friesland and northern Noord-Holland, and pre-treats water transported to Heemskerk/Bergen and the dunes.

PWN reports about 24 million m³/year directly produced and more than 45 million m³/year pre-treated at Andijk; its 2025/2026 scoping material describes maximum WPJ and PS Andijk process capacities. Annual/design values are not live intake, storage, quality, delivered flow, backup or restoration.

PWN identifies water availability, source quality, chloride/salinity, ecology, energy and future demand as planning drivers. IJsselmeer water also supports regional level management, agriculture and industry, so drinking-water intake, polder supply and emergency allocation are distinct pathways.

The public pages publish context but not security-sensitive full pipe topology, current plant state, reserve, dependency switching or recovery. Reuse licence and machine operational cadence are not stated; live assertions require operator-authorized evidence.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Road, transit and external acute-care dependencies
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; OVapi snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Ten monthly CC0 NWB border records reduce to A7, N307, N241, N239, N240 and N505 physical identities connecting Hollands Kroon, Drechterland, Hoorn, Opmeer and Koggenland. Repeated A7/N307/N240 sides are series/shared corridors, not independent additive capacity; 260/150 values are scenario units.

A7 and N307 are cross-municipal backbones; N239/N240/N241/N505 serve dispersed villages, farms, glasshouses, the IJsselmeer shore and external destinations. Static geometry does not establish junction, bridge, dike-road, closure, congestion, detour or evacuation state.

No ProRail station lies inside GM0420. The 112 in-boundary GTFS stop areas include Medemblik and Abbekerk bus stations, but schedules/locations do not prove live buses, accessible capacity, staff, fuel, evacuation or supply transport.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 has no emergency department in GM0420; Dijklander Ziekenhuis Hoorn is the nearest registry record and reports 24/7 emergency care, fifteen rooms and 21,650 visits in 2025. The questionnaire and proximity do not establish route time, ambulance access, acceptance, occupancy, staffing, backup or diversion.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Medemblik / Liander / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Glasshouse/agricultural demand and partial electricity, communication and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Het Grootslag agreement published 31 August 2026; public-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: The municipality identifies Het Grootslag as a nationally important glasshouse cluster using geothermal heat and a local heat network and says future work must address energy infrastructure, grid congestion, water provision and access. This is current economic/dependency context, not incident load or continuity.

One NBNL postcode sample maps to Liander area OS WESTWOUD 10-4i and reports 30 MW existing versus 49 MW required withdrawal/injection, queues, 33 projects and earliest year 2026. The open-data planning sample is not full municipal coverage, a current outage, live load, reserve, switching or restoration; exact dataset licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns 86 installations—one broadcast, seventeen fixed-link, 35 mobile, two other-mobile and 31 amateur—and DUO assigns 30 education locations—23 primary, one secondary and six other registered uses. RDI has no stated standard licence/fixed cadence; DUO is attribution-licensed and daily.

Public points and planning areas do not establish telecom coverage/backhaul/power, school occupancy/support role, glasshouse demand, seasonal labour, food-chain stock, operator state, backup or recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Regional all-hazard context and time-bound monitoring gaps
evidenceSources.edition: VRNHN current crisis pages and 2022 risk-profile status confirmed by 15 March 2024 board papers; monitoring snapshots 2–3 September 2026
supports: VRNHN's current/public planning covers flood, vital-service loss, extreme weather, care continuity, gas transport, water incidents, nature fire, vulnerable-building fire, hazardous materials, major traffic and animal disease. Regional eligibility is not a GM0420 event probability, footprint or current warning.

No KNMI weather station, RIVM PM2.5 point, recent KNMI seismic origin or Waterinfo point is assigned inside the administrative polygon. Nearest weather points include Wijdenes/Berkhout; Krabbersgat is an IJsselmeer Waterinfo point outside municipal assignment. Neighbouring points are not local continuous surfaces.

At 2 September 2026 17:30Z Krabbersgat reported -24 cm and the rolling public forecast provides -28/-25/-25/-25 cm for T+1/+6/+12/+24. These CC0 station/datum/time values are public non-mission-critical context, not a selected defence event or municipal inundation field; no T+48/+72 feature is present.

Canonical wildfire is remote Veluwe smoke, earthquake is a remote Groningen exercise and cyber has no named target. Absence of local observations or modeled forcing is not zero local weather, smoke, ground susceptibility, cyber exposure or safety.

findings.summary: A real IJsselmeer flood pathway is presented as an unsupported generic coastal metre field and all-clear.
findings.evidence: E02/E03 distinguish IJsselmeer boundary conditions, multiple primary/regional defences and pumped polders. The model selects none but asserts 1.556982 m T+6–24, 21,980 affected and 457,998.188 person-hours at T+24, then zero flood at T+48 despite 20,115 affected and T+72 burden 1,390,963.604.
findings.action: V3 release gate: require an expert-selected IJsselmeer level/wind-wave scenario, defence trajectory/state and breach/overtopping, connected versioned LIWO footprint, probability, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, uncertainty, NoData and HHNK/WMCN review. Suppress metre/affected/service/all-clear claims until selected.

findings.summary: Eight materially different nonzero hazards reuse one complete 61-neighbourhood rank.

findings.action: Replace the common rank with hazard-specific full-geometry evidence surfaces and explicit coverage/NoData. Add regressions for source containment, connected hydraulic footprint, different mechanism order and shoreline generalization while preserving service-layer invariance.

findings.summary: The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset imposes direct local depth without a relevant Medemblik source contract.

findings.action: Suppress direct GM0420 river depth. Retain only separately labeled upstream/regional supply, road or IJsselmeer-management dependencies with evidence; any direct inundation requires a selected connected official water/defence scenario rather than the generic river preset.

findings.summary: Generic water/drainage scores omit the causal coupling of defences, electric polder drainage and PWN Andijk drinking water.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat, WMCN, HHNK, PWN, VRNHN, municipality, hospital or operator forecast, warning, probability, evacuation order, casualty estimate or restoration promise.
No selected IJsselmeer level/wave, defence trajectory/state, breach/overtopping, connected LIWO footprint, probability, depth/velocity/arrival/recession or NoData mask is ingested for GM0420.

The coastal 1.556982 m and river 0.462165 m properties are synthetic screening values, not observed or officially modeled local metres and must not drive evacuation, routes, care, intake or pump thresholds.

The generalized boundary does not resolve shoreline, dikes, polders, levels, catchments, buildings, drains, roads, assets, households or individuals; Andijk/Medemblik BAG point mismatches remain version/generalization warnings.
CBS neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed; the -4 population difference and null district-heat, charging and other fields are publication semantics, not missing/zero people or assets.
HWH is partial and its 285 points do not prove complete topology, compatible units, control, telemetry, power, backup or restoration; null/zero retains source semantics.
Vier Noorder Koggen and PWN published capacities are design/context values, not measured T+0 availability, delivered flow, reserve, quality or recovery.
No complete public PWN pipe/intake/storage, Liander feeder/switching, gas, municipal sewer or telecom backhaul/restoration topology is authorized in the model.
One NBNL postcode sample is planning/queue context rather than full municipal coverage, current load, outage, reserve, switching or restoration.
RDI sites do not establish coverage, traffic, backhaul, power/backup, damage, availability or restoration; standard reuse licence/fixed cadence is unstated.

NWB and GTFS are static context and do not establish incident-time road/bus throughput, evacuation, responder, pump/intake repair, care or supply continuity; repeated corridor records are not additive.
RIVM acute-care questionnaire data does not establish Dijklander route time, acceptance, occupancy, staffing, diversion, medicines, water, generator fuel or backup endurance.
DUO locations do not establish command, reception, shelter, care or distribution roles; the municipality's support-point locations are still a 2026 pilot.
No local KNMI weather, RIVM PM2.5, Waterinfo or recent seismic point is assigned; neighbouring Wijdenes/Berkhout/Krabbersgat values are not continuous municipal fields or forecasts through T+72.
Krabbersgat values are point/datum/time-specific and public non-mission-critical; absence at T+48/+72 is NoData, not zero IJsselmeer water or defence safety.
Canonical wildfire lacks local ignition/perimeter/fuel/plume; earthquake is remote Groningen; cyber lacks named target/architecture/detection; compound mixes unvalidated assumptions.
Ports, boating/recreation, historic-building/foundation vulnerability, agriculture, glasshouses, seasonal labour, food logistics and salinity/water-quality allocation are not fully represented.
Household three-day guidance is a preparedness horizon, not measured stock, guaranteed aid arrival, equality of access or a recovery deadline.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not measured outage-hours, simultaneous deprivation, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid change and 72 hours excludes prolonged flooding, salinity, drought and reconstruction.
